# LAST LIGHT: a cinematic 3D product film (10 s, 1920×1080, 24 fps)

**Idea (one sentence):** a turntable (fictional brand ORRERY, Model One) in a dark room as the last sun comes through a window in a hazy shaft. The film is about the moment before music: a clock ticks, the arm lifts and swings out, the stylus descends in silence, and the music starts on contact as the camera cranes back to reveal the object in its beam of light.

**Files:** `lastlight.mp4`, `lastlight.json` (spec, generated by `film.py`), `score.json` (made by `score.py`), `contact.jpg`, `GAPS.md`.

## References (gathered first; compared side by side at full size)

| Reference | Source | What I took |
|---|---|---|
| Roger Deakins, *Blade Runner 2049* (2017) | https://film-grab.com/2019/05/24/blade-runner-2049/ | One hard motivated source; silhouettes against lit haze; most of the frame allowed to fall to black. |
| Roger Deakins, *The Assassination of Jesse James* (2007) | https://film-grab.com/2010/06/17/the-assassination-of-jesse-james-by-the-coward-robert-ford/ | Low golden-hour sun as the key; warm against cool ambient. |
| Paul Thomas Anderson, *Phantom Thread* (2017) | https://film-grab.com/2019/03/27/phantom-thread/ | Window light on objects, craft and close attention to hands and material. |
| Wong Kar-wai / Christopher Doyle, *In the Mood for Love* (2000) | https://film-grab.com/2013/03/09/in-the-mood-for-love/ | Deep reds against shadow; frames that hold on texture and anticipation. |
| Vermeer, *The Milkmaid* (c. 1658) | https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Johannes_Vermeer_-_Het_melkmeisje_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg | A single window as the whole lighting design; the quiet moment before an action. |

**What makes them great:** every light has a reason; darkness is used, not avoided; the camera stays close to material and action (macro, shallow focus, slow purposeful moves); sound and silence carry the tension.

## Shots
1. **0–2.4 s, establishing, 35 mm, into the sun:** the source fans through the haze, dust drifts, the turntable is a silhouette with its arm parked; a clock ticks once a second. (An earlier cut opened top-down on the spinning record, at a true 33⅓ = 200°/s, with the label text curving around the spindle via the polar-mapped surface; it was the weakest frame, so it was replaced.)
2. **2.4–4.2 s, low behind the arm, into the sun:** the tonearm lifts (cue-lever click) and swings out over the record in silhouette against the shaft; strobe dots on the platter rim.
3. **4.2–6.4 s, record level, 85 mm:** the stylus descends; the gap of light between the cartridge and the label closes; the tick stops; near silence.
4. **6.4–10 s, crane back with a slow zoom-out (75 → 38 mm):** contact. Crackle and hiss start under a Db major 9 piano chord and strings as the camera pulls back to reveal the turntable in its shaft of light; ORRERY / MODEL ONE · MADE TO BE LISTENED TO.

## Engine features used
Ray-traced `scene3d` (`night` env, custom spot as the sun with `fog.shafts`), custom geometry (a parametric `surface` disc textured with a polar-unwrapped groove/label composition), instanced strobe dots, expression-driven tonearm rotation and lift (a tube `path` of `s` and `t`), real DOF and focal lengths per shot, a walnut composition on the plinth face, and a score with custom noise synths (crackle, hiss), woodblock clock ticks, Salamander piano and strings, plus sfx clicks.
